did_you_know.text: Did you know that Micah reminds the rulers of Jacob and the leaders of Israel that they are responsible for knowing justice—that is, understanding it and acting justly?
Did you know that Micah describes the leaders as hating good and loving evil, turning moral values upside down?
Did you know that the prophet uses the vivid image of eating flesh to describe how the leaders oppress and exploit the people?
Did you know that Micah warns that when these oppressive leaders cry out to the LORD, he will not answer them but will hide his face from them—a fitting response to their evil deeds?
Did you know that Micah accuses the prophets of proclaiming peace to anyone who supports them, but declaring war on anyone who gives them nothing?
Did you know that the punishment of the misleading prophets is described as night, darkness, and the setting of the sun—images symbolizing the loss of vision and guidance?
Did you know that the seers and diviners will be ashamed and cover their lips because they will receive no answer from God?

Did you know that Micah presents his prophetic authority as coming from being filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and courage, so that he can expose Jacob’s crimes and Israel’s sins?

Did you know that Micah describes a corrupt public system in which rulers judge for bribes, priests teach for a fee, and prophets practice divination for money, while all of them still claim that the LORD is among them?

Did you know that at the end of the chapter Micah prophesies that, because of the leaders’ corruption, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become ruins, and the Temple Mount will become a wooded height?
